chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Singing with her uncle's group and early performing history
summary: The job lasted a while; she just went along for the ride; she recaps her early appearances and when singing developed.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I don't know. I don't know. But they had -- this job must have lasted about three months or something like that in Steubenville, Ohio, they worked at a tavern there, and of course I went to Steubenville with them, so therefore I sang

every night. But I was just -- you know, went along for the ride. Some nights I'd work and some nights I wouldn't. You know, I wasn't employed by the band. They had guest singers used to come in from New York or maybe from Pittsburgh, they had names that they would feature at the club. But this was more or less a tavern, a local tavern.
And these were my earlier experiences, you know, singing around with a group.
Can we go back over your career -- your performing career, your performing history?
First, is the famous incident when you sang the 'Chinese Blues' in church. Then you, in 1918 --
Sang 'I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles' at Carnegie Library.
And then how did it begin to develop after that?
It didn't. It didn't develop until I got much older, you know, after I came out of high school, as I said before, I got little odd jobs around -- waiting tables or taking
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

care of somebody's house or something like that. And locally, if there was an affair, a dance, or a club that had a band, I'd probably drop in and sing a few songs. I was popular as a singer around there, but I was just singing for kicks, more or less.

And it wasn't actually until Harry came back from off the road that I probably got interested enough to want to go further as a singer. I never had any idea that anything would come of it. I certainly didn't think of singing to make a living at it until I probably wound up with Harry in Steubenville, Ohio, which was around 1933-34, something like that. Which is pretty late. I spent a lot of years in between doing nothing by way of a singing career. Just little odd jobs around.
Do you remember the songs you sang?

Mmm, let me see, well, whatever was popular at that time I guess I was singing. "All of Me" you know, "Stars Fell on Alabama," whatever was currently popular. I had nothing special to sing, and as I said before, I just went along for
